name: Mind Melt gives its debuff a 15 second life (#2165)
contract: Mind Melt 572771's tooltip reads "Damage dealt by Melt Reality now also reduces the target's primary attributes by $572851s2% for $/1000;s1 sec, stacking $572851u times." In Spell.dbc the talent is a single SPELL_AURA_ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER (107) with EffectMiscValue 1 (SPELLMOD_DURATION), EffectBasePoints 14999 + DieSides 1 = +15000 ms, EffectSpellClassMask [0,0,262144], which inside SpellFamilyName 28 selects the Mind Melt debuff 572851. 572851 has DurationIndex 0, so SpellInfo::GetDuration returns 0, not -1; Player::IsAffectedBySpellmod only blocks duration modifiers on spells whose duration is -1 (Player.cpp), and Aura::CalcMaxDuration then yields 0 + 15000 = 15000 ms (SpellAuras.cpp). Without the talent the debuff would expire immediately, so the talent is what gives it a life. Its payload is 572851's Effect[1], SPELL_AURA_MOD_TOTAL_STAT_PERCENTAGE (137) with EffectMiscValue -1 (all stats) and EffectBasePoints -4 + DieSides 1 = -3%, with StackAmount 5. Every Melt Reality rank (503895-503899, 572835, 806335) carries EffectTriggerSpell 572851 on a SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_TRIGGER_SPELL effect, so the debuff is applied by the Melt Reality caster and takes that caster's modifiers. Generic core machinery. This scenario is a regression guard for behaviour that already works.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
The debuff's own duration before the talent
Untalented, the debuff has no duration at all
The debuff's attribute payload is -3% per stack either way
That is exactly +15000 ms against the baseline
Fixture the debuff at its five-stack cap
Five stacks reduce every stat by 15%
